description.summary: the overview's control of workspaces and of their windows

protocol.description:
What the overview needs of the workspaces of ext-workspace-v1 and of the windows of ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1 beyond those protocols: a workspace's pinned state, its pin and its place among its output's workspaces; each window's workspace, its place on the outputs and its move to another workspace; and the ext-image-copy-capture-v1 source of a workspace, for its thumbnail. The compositor offers the manager only to the clients it trusts with it; it is Athanor's own protocol (doc_own_stack.md OS5, decision 32).
Every request of athanor_workspace_v1 and athanor_workspace_window_v1 does nothing, with no protocol error, while the session is locked or paused on another virtual terminal, on a handle that went away, and on a window that is neither minimised nor drawn and placed.
A new version adds interfaces, requests, events or enum entries; a client binds the version it knows.

interface.name: athanor_workspace_manager_v1
interface.description: Makes the object of a workspace, the object of a window and the capture source of a workspace.

entry.name: already_made
entry.summary: the client already has an object of this workspace or of this window

request.name: destroy
request.description: The objects and the sources made from the manager stay valid.

request.name: get_workspace
request.description: Makes the object of the workspace an ext_workspace_handle_v1 stands for. Its state and its capabilities are sent at once; for a workspace already removed, removed is sent instead. A second object of the same workspace, while the client holds a first that was not sent removed, is the already_made error.

request.name: get_workspace_window
request.description: Makes the object of the window an ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 stands for. Its workspace, its places and a done event are sent at once, then each change followed by done. On a closed handle the object is inert: it sends nothing. A second object of the same window, while the client holds the first, is the already_made error.

request.name: get_capture_source

description.summary: the capture source of a workspace

request.description: Makes the ext-image-copy-capture-v1 source of the workspace an ext_workspace_handle_v1 stands for, active or not. Its frames have the size of the workspace's output in pixels, its mode, and that output's transform. They hold the workspace's windows as that output draws them, each with its marks: the confined border, the focus outline and the divider ring. They never hold the pointer, nor any layer surface: behind the windows the frame is transparent, and an empty workspace gives a transparent frame. While the session is locked, and once the workspace is gone, a session of the source is refused and its frames fail.

interface.name: athanor_workspace_v1
interface.description: A workspace's pinned state and capabilities, sent when the object is made and at each change, whatever made it, and the requests that pin it and move it among its output's workspaces. The order of the workspaces is the coordinates ext-workspace-v1 sends.

entry.name: pinned
entry.summary: the workspace is kept when it empties, for the rest of the session

event.name: state
event.description: Every flag that holds; a flag absent no longer holds. A new workspace is not pinned.

event.name: capabilities

description.summary: what the workspace's requests can do

event.description: Every workspace can be pinned. The empty workspace each output keeps last cannot move, and is sent without move; it is sent move once it is no longer last.

event.name: removed
event.description: The workspace was removed. The object sends nothing more and ignores its requests; the client destroys it.

request.name: pin
request.description: Pins the workspace: it is not removed when its last window leaves it, for the rest of the session. Nothing is stored on disk. Every object of the workspace is then sent state.

request.name: unpin

description.summary: let the workspace go when it empties

request.description: Unpins the workspace: an empty workspace that is neither active nor last is then removed, as any emptied workspace is. Every object of the workspace is sent state, or removed.

request.name: move_before
request.description: Places the workspace just before the workspace other stands for, among the workspaces of its output. It is refused, and changes nothing, when other is a workspace of another output, and when the workspace cannot move.

request.name: move_after
request.description: Places the workspace just after the workspace other stands for, among the workspaces of its output. It is refused, and changes nothing, when other is a workspace of another output, when other is the empty workspace kept last, and when the workspace cannot move.

interface.name: athanor_workspace_window_v1
interface.description: The workspace a window is on and its place on each output, sent as what changed at each frame, and the request that moves it to another workspace. Events are applied together at done.

event.name: workspace_enter

description.summary: the window is on a workspace

event.description: Sent only to a client that holds the ext_workspace_handle_v1 of that workspace.

description.summary: the window is no longer on a workspace

event.name: geometry

description.summary: the window's place on an output

event.description: The window's geometry on output, in logical pixels, x and y relative to that output's top left. A window shown is sent for each output it overlaps; a window on an inactive workspace, or minimised, is sent the place it keeps, on its workspace's output. A width or a height of zero withdraws the window from that output.

description.summary: the events since the last done apply

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move the window to a workspace

request.description: Moves the window to the workspace an ext_workspace_handle_v1 stands for, on output: a window moved to an inactive workspace leaves the screen, and one moved to another output's workspace is centred there. A minimised window stays minimised. It is refused, and changes nothing, when output is not the workspace's own.
